TimeIndex::resample_count¶

Back to TimeIndex API Reference

Signatures¶

TimeIndex::resample_count(const ResampleOptions& options) const -> pluss::Series
TimeIndex::resample_count(std::string_view freq, std::int64_t step = 1) const -> pluss::Series

What It Does¶

Counts how many observations land in each resampling bin.

This is the “size per bucket” form of resampling. It does not require a second values vector because it counts the timestamps themselves.

It is often the best first diagnostic on a new time axis because it tells you whether the regrouping logic itself is producing the buckets you think it is.

Parameters¶

freq

The base bin frequency such as "H", "D", "min", or "S".

step

How many freq units each bin spans.

options

The full resampling control block. See resample_bins for the detailed meaning of closed, label, origin, and offset_nanos.

If the counts already look wrong, the problem is usually the axis or the resample options rather than the later value aggregation.

Returns¶

pluss::Series A 1D numeric Series containing one count per resample bin.

Examples¶

Example 1. Count how many observations land in each hourly bin.

auto counts = idx.resample_count("H");
std::cout << pluss::series::print(counts) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 2]

Example 2. Increase step when you want each bin to span multiple base frequency units.

auto counts = idx.resample_count("H", 2);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(counts) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[5]

Notes¶

  • resample_count() is the direct answer to “how many rows did I observe per interval?”

  • It is axis-only, so no secondary payload is needed.

  • If you also need output labels, pair it with resample_bins.
